text:
elaine: heads up — after the RBAC refactor deploy earlier today, an on-prem admin reported they were able to modify VPC allowlists from the private control plane UI. not good :grimacing:
matt: wait — they shouldn't have the network.write permission anymore. which role did they have?
sre-jordan: infra-bot shows they were in group 'onprem-admins' which got a new composite role binding during the refactor. could be precedence bug.
elaine: exact symptom: user added a CIDR to an allowlist and the change went through, but audit logs show no role_binding.create event for that change. only the network.change entry.
sec-audit: weird — audit pipeline should record role bindings and who approved them. did the refactor change the audit webhook config?
leah: i checked the helm diff earlier — we swapped to the new rbac-controller v2 and replaced direct rolebindings with role-sets. might have missed emitting "rbac.audit" events.
matt: infra-bot — link to the deploy?
infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T14:02Z: rbac-controller v2.1.0 -> rolled to private control plane clusters: pc-01, pc-02.
sre-jordan: reproduction steps I'm running now:
```bash
# emulate user in onprem-admins
kubectl auth can-i update networkpolicy --as=user:alice --namespace=redwood-private
# attempt to patch allowlist
kubectl patch configmap vpc-allowlist -p '{"data":{"cidrs":"10.0.0.0/8,192.168.0.0/16"}}' --as=user:alice
```
leah: logs show the patch succeeded and returned 200. the controller emitted network.change but no role.set or binding audit line.
sec-audit: are audit logs stored encrypted with KMS? if so maybe the signing step failed and events were dropped.
matt: KMS integration was untouched in this deploy. but we did move the audit forwarder into the control plane process. could be a race where forwarder starts after rbac controller, losing early events.
elaine: immediate mitigation: revoke 'onprem-admins' elevated composite role and put them back on legacy rolebinding until we fix. can someone run the revoke?
sre-jordan: running revoke now. patch: `kubectl delete rolebinding onprem-admins-composite -n redwood-private`
infra-bot: rolebinding onprem-admins-composite deleted (request by sre-jordan).
leah: policy test: after revoke, alice can no longer patch allowlist. good.
matt: we need two fixes: 1) make RBAC controller emit explicit audit events (and ensure forwarder handles them), 2) add an owner check on control-plane UI to block allowlist edits unless explicit network.admin role.
sec-audit: also add a validation in the audit ingestion that rejects gaps — if we see network.change without a preceding role_binding grant/approve within X seconds, open an alert. could surface false positives but useful for now.
sre-jordan: agree. i'll open an incident ticket and triage. putting proposed labels: severity=high, impacted=private-control-plane, mitigation=revoke-binding, action=postmortem.
matt: KMS note — when we re-enable the forwarder, ensure it does envelope encryption on audit batches and signs with the KMS key. also rotate the forwarder service identity so previous dropped events can't be replayed.
leah: quick patch diff I'm suggesting (pseudo):
```diff
- controller.emit(network.change)
+ controller.emit(rbac.audit, actor, role_changes)
+ controller.emit(network.change)
```
elaine: also can we add an offline audit dump export to GCS/S3 for private customers? if forwarder fails we still have backups.
sec-audit: yes — add periodic checkpoint snapshots encrypted with KMS. we already have S3 bucket redwood-audit-archive in us-west-2, need bucket policy update for private-ctl plane accounts.
matt: assign tasks: sre-jordan -> incident ticket + revoke check (done). leah -> PR for audit emission and forwarder retry. sec-audit -> alert rule for 'orphan network changes'. elaine -> customer comms + temporary ACL check added to UI. I'll handle KMS verification and rotation plan.
leah: PR opened: https://git.redwood.dev/r/rbac/controller/pulls/482 — adds audit events and retries on forwarder failure.
sre-jordan: incident created: INC-2026-0318-01 (link in #incidents). added timeline and initial mitigation notes.
elaine: customer impacted: customer-acme on pc-02; notified via SOC at 14:22Z.
sec-audit: postmortem checklist: root cause (rbac-controller v2 mixing role-sets without audit hooks), detection gap (audit forwarder startup race + no orphan-change alert), blast radius (pc-02 allowlist altered once), remediation (revert binding pattern, add audits, KMS signing, export snapshots), timeline, follow-ups.
matt: added follow-up: add unit tests that assert audit events emitted for every role-related mutation. no silent failures.
leah: also adding e2e test: spin up control plane with forwarder failing and ensure events are checkpointed to disk for retry.
elaine: thanks all. once PR merges we'll schedule a canary roll to pc-01 first and watch audit ingestion metrics. :thumbsup:
sec-audit: leaving this thread in case we need to attach logs — i'll paste the raw snippet below:
```
2026-03-18T14:05:12Z INFO rbac-controller: applied role-set onprem-admins -> roles:[onprem.read,onprem.exec]
2026-03-18T14:05:13Z INFO controller: network.change user=alice target=vpc-allowlist:added=10.8.0.0/24
2026-03-18T14:05:13Z WARN audit-forwarder: no connection to kms://key/redwood-audit-signing, buffering 1 events
2026-03-18T14:05:14Z INFO controller: network.change applied status=200
```
elaine: good — that shows the warning. sec-audit, plz add that to the incident timeline.
sec-audit: added. tagging: @matt @leah @sre-jordan. we'll aim for patch rollback window 2h, full fix in 48h.
matt: thanks team. closing temporary ACL after fixes and will follow up with postmortem draft tomorrow. :lock:
